cards.explanation: The answer is three, friends. Abraham looks up and sees three men standing nearby (Genesis 18:2). That's quite a crowd to show up at one tent in the heat of the day. Hold on to that number, because Abraham is about to get very busy.

The answer is True! Abraham was sitting at the entrance of his tent in the heat of the day (Genesis 18:1). Then he spots three men, and he runs to meet them and bows low to the ground (Genesis 18:2). Sitting to sprinting, just like that. I get winded reaching for a cooling rack, and this man is off like somebody yelled FRESH BATCH.

The answer is water to wash their feet, friends. Abraham says, “Let a little water be brought, that you may wash your feet and rest yourselves under the tree.” (Genesis 18:4). Travelers in the heat would want that, I bet. Offering a rest and a wash before anything else is a warm way to say welcome.

The answer is bread, friends. Abraham says, “And I will bring a bit of bread so that you may refresh yourselves.” (Genesis 18:5). Notice he calls it a bit. Hold on to that word, because this meal gets a lot bigger as the passage goes on.

The answer is a tender and choice calf. Genesis 18:7 says Abraham ran to the herd, selected one, and gave it to a servant, who hurried to prepare it. Remember he only promised a bit of bread. Now there's a whole calf involved, and I think Abraham is just getting started.

The answer is False, friends. Abraham brought the curds, the milk and the prepared calf, set them before the men, and stood by them under the tree as they ate (Genesis 18:8). He serves and he stays close. The text never has him sit down to eat.

The question they ask is, “Where is your wife Sarah?” (Genesis 18:9). Abraham answers, “There, in the tent…” They ask about Sarah by name, friends. I think that question is worth noticing, because of what comes next.

The answer is True, and it's big news, friends. The LORD says, “I will surely return to you at this time next year, and your wife Sarah will have a son!” (Genesis 18:10). The promise comes with a time attached: this time next year. And Sarah is right there, listening at the entrance to the tent.

The answer is laughs, friends. Genesis 18:12 says, “So she laughed to herself…” She's been listening at the entrance to the tent and she hears this news (Genesis 18:10). I think a quiet laugh like that is hard to hold back when the news sounds impossible.
The answer is Abraham, friends. Genesis 18:13 says the LORD asked Abraham, “Why did Sarah laugh…” Sarah laughed to herself, and the LORD still brings it up. Abraham is the one who gets the question.

The point is that nothing is too difficult for the LORD, friends. He asks, “Is anything too difficult for the LORD?” (Genesis 18:14). Then He repeats the promise: He will return at the appointed time, and Sarah will have a son. Sarah heard something that sounded impossible, and He answers it with that question.
What Sarah says is, “I did not laugh.” Genesis 18:15 tells us Sarah was afraid, so she denied it. I think anybody caught like that would grab for a quick answer, friends.

The answer is True, friends. The LORD replies, “No… but you did laugh.” (Genesis 18:15). He says it plainly, and nothing in the text shows Him raising His voice. Sarah said she didn't laugh, and He answers her right there.
